extracted.intended_audience: historians, students and scholars of advertising and print-media history; practitioners interested in origins of newspaper advertising
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and primary-source guidance on what early (17th-century English) advertising-papers should publish, how often and how they should be distributed; plus examples of typical ad content and business models of that era.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication frequency and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Bills of Advertisements ... shall come out every week on Thursday morning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The circular specifies a weekly schedule (Thursday morning) for the Mercury / Bills of Advertisements, establishing regularity of publication to reach readers on a fixed day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution channels and delivery points
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivered and dispersed in every house where the Bills of Mortality are received, and elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribute copies widely and systematically — to houses receiving official registers (Bills of Mortality), booksellers, shops, inns, coffee-houses, and to most cities and principal towns — to maximise readership and local penetration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / permissible subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The Publications and Advertisements of all the matters following, or any other matter or thing ... that shall relate to the Advancemejit of Trade, or any lawful business not granted in propriety to any other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper is intended to publish anything pertaining to promotion of trade or lawful business (i.e., a broad commercial remit), excluding matters already monopolised by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sales notices: goods, merchandise, ships for sale — required particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of all Goods, Merchandizes, and Ships to be sold, the place where to be seen, and day and hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sale advertisements should state what is for sale and provide precise practical details: where the purchaser can inspect the item and the day and hour for viewing or sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freight/charter advertisements: essential information
rubrics_metrics.description: Any ships to be let to Freight, and the time of their departure, the place of the Master's habitation, and where to be spoken with before and after Exchange time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freight notices must include departure time and a concrete contact location for the master (where he can be found before/after exchange hours) so prospective shippers can arrange business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ship particulars for shipping notices
rubrics_metrics.description: All Ships, their Names, and Burthens, and capacities, and where their Inventaries are to be seen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shipping advertisements should list ship name, tonnage/burthen and capacity, and the location where the ship's inventory can be inspected, giving buyers/charterers full information to evaluate suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parcels, materials, and furniture for shipping
rubrics_metrics.description: All other Parcels and Materials or Furniture for shipping in like manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other goods intended for shipment should be advertised with the same level of detail as ships and merchandize (place, viewing time, contact), enabling efficient commercial arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content categories to be carried (general list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Titles of books, houses or land to be lett or sold, persons removing from one place to another, things lost or stole, physitians' advertisements, or inquiries for houses or for servants, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper should accept a wide variety of commercial and personal notices: book announcements, property for sale/let, change of address notices, lost/stolen items, medical/physician adverts, and servant/employee inquiries — reflecting everyday needs of trade and society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Free-copy / distribution strategy funded by advertisers
rubrics_metrics.description: The scheme of issuing sheets of advertisements gratuitously, trusting for profit to the number of advertisers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers could give away printed advertising sheets (free to readers/shops/coffee-houses) and derive revenue from selling ad space to many advertisers — an early ad-funded circulation model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted placement to maximise readership
rubrics_metrics.description: He gives away every Monday above a thousand of them to all the Booksellers, shops and inns, and most of the principal coffee-houses in London and Westminster. Besides they are now sent to most of the cities and principal towns in England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concentrate free distribution to high-footfall, reading-oriented locations (booksellers, inns, coffee-houses) and send copies to other towns to increase advertiser reach; one copy can be read by many people, making this cost-effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative advantage over street bills
rubrics_metrics.description: This way of publishing is much more advantageous than giving away Bills in the street, ... a thousand of these cannot be supposed to be read by less than twenty times the number of persons, and done for at least the twentieth part of the charge, and with much less trouble and greater success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers should use printed weekly sheets rather than handbills in the street because a single distributed paper is re-read multiple times by different people, yielding far greater impressions per copy and lower cost per reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic differentiation for ad classes
rubrics_metrics.description: Booksellers' and quacks' advertisements ... always preceded the others, and were printed in a different type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different classes of adverts (e.g., booksellers, medical practitioners) were given typographic prominence or distinct type and ordered ahead of other notices — an editorial/layout practice to distinguish categories and perhaps signal importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport/service ads: include schedules and rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage Coaches ... for the Rates and at the times hereafter mentioned and declared. Every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday. To Salisbury in two days for xxs. ... Once every fortnight to Edinburgh for ivs. a peece — Mondays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Travel/coach advertisements should give explicit departure days, routes, trip durations and fares, so travellers can plan and compare services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of rewards and precise physical descriptions in recovery/runaway notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Runaway and lost-person advertisements list rewards and detailed physical/clothing descriptions (e.g., pock-marked, dress, age) to aid capture or recovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lost/runaway notices should offer a reward and give detailed identifying information (age, complexion, clothing, marks, distinguishing features) plus where to report to increase chances of recovery; examples show exhaustive physical descriptions used as identification.
